topic.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Learning and System Resilience
topic.overview: Cooperative reinforcement learning asks several agents to discover behavior that works well collectively. These papers study shared information, policy regularization, value aggregation, and exploration across a joint action space. A representative method encourages coordination through predictable actions or synchronized behavior selection, giving independently acting agents useful structure for exploring team strategies.
topic.whyItMatters: Individually reasonable choices can fail when success requires coordinated timing or complementary roles. As teams scale, evaluation must also consider communication limits, decentralized decisions, and the disproportionate impact that failure of a few agents may have.
topic.evolution: Early representatives compare independent and cooperative learning and apply collective intelligence to routing. Later work develops multi-agent actor–critic methods and systematic cooperative benchmarks. Recent research examines uncertainty-aware value aggregation, richer coordination policies, and identifying agents whose failures most damage system performance.
openQuestions: How can coordination remain effective when team composition changes?
What training strategies reduce dependence on a small set of critical agents without sacrificing collective performance?

papers.title: Learning Disentangled Multi-Agent World Model for Decentralized Control
papers.tldr: DMAWM separates individual agent representations from shared interaction dynamics to improve learning and transfer for decentralized control.

papers.title: Learning Human-Robot Collaboration via Heterogeneous-Agent Lyapunov Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: HALO stabilizes decentralized human–robot policy learning by adjusting gradients to contract the gap from cooperative optimization.

papers.title: Learning Multi-Agent Coordination via Sheaf-ADMM
papers.tldr: Sheaf-ADMM trains locally informed agents to coordinate through explicit optimization constraints, improving reported robustness and Sudoku solving.

papers.title: Learning Robust Multi-Agent Policies via Selective Adversarial Fault Induction
papers.tldr: MARTA improves cooperative-agent robustness by learning when to induce malfunctions and how faulty agents should behave during training.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Communication for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: LMAC uses a language model to refine communication protocols that improve agents’ shared understanding and cooperative performance.

papers.title: MAFE: Enabling Equitable Algorithm Design in Multi-Agent Multi-Stage Decision-Making Systems
papers.tldr: MAFE supplies multi-agent simulations for studying how sequential decisions create fairness, performance, and coordination trade-offs.

papers.title: MEAL: A Benchmark for Continual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: MEAL makes 100-task continual multi-agent reinforcement-learning evaluations practical and reveals failures hidden by shorter task sequences.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Submodular Reward
papers.tldr: Submodular team rewards enable cooperative reinforcement-learning algorithms with polynomial optimization and provable approximation and regret guarantees.

papers.title: Offline Multi-agent Continual Cooperation via Skill Partition and Reuse
papers.tldr: COMAD continually discovers, expands, and reuses coordination skills from offline data to improve transfer across sequential multi-agent tasks.

papers.title: Phase-Aware Mixture of Experts for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: PA-MoE learns task-phase boundaries and routes coherent stretches of agent behavior to the same expert to support specialization.

papers.title: Scalable Traffic Signal Control with Shared Policy Framework
papers.tldr: SLight adaptively shares traffic-control principles across intersections and sustains reported performance gains as networks grow.

papers.title: Scaling Multi-Agent Environment Co-Design with Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: DiCoDe uses constrained diffusion guidance and critic distillation to jointly improve multi-agent policies and environment designs.

papers.title: Secure Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Service Systems with Affinity and Byzantine Nodes: Stability Analysis and Protection Design
papers.tldr: A resilient consensus-based learning algorithm limits malicious parameter interference and provides conditional guarantees for traffic stability and approximate policy convergence.

papers.title: Sparse Topology-Aware Pairwise Scoring for Large-Scale Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: SOPS combines a scalable communication backbone with learned sparse links to improve cooperation across multi-agent benchmarks.

papers.title: TACTIC: Task-Aware Sparse Coordination Graphs for Multi-Task Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: TACTIC uses discrete task semantics to adapt sparse coordination graphs and condition local policies in multi-agent learning.

papers.title: Towards Complete Multi-Agent Coordination Policy Learning via Denoising Maximum Entropy Optimization
papers.tldr: Dspic combines learned agent roles with a shared diffusion policy to improve efficient coordination across heterogeneous agents.

papers.title: Value Aggregation with Uncertainty in Online Decentralized MARL
papers.tldr: Uncertainty-aware Q-value aggregation addresses learning rollback and provides convergence and variance guarantees for decentralized multi-agent policy evaluation.

papers.title: Vulnerable Agent Identification in Large-Scale Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A hierarchical method identifies which agents can cause the worst system failures by separating agent selection from adversarial policy learning.
